near_miss_corrected.what_happened: The first check implementation used 'virt-install --print-xml 9'. In virt-install, a step number selects WHICH install phase XML to print, and bare --print-xml still performs storage creation unless --dry-run is given.

host_finding_vm_pool_unencrypted.severity: recorded risk, independent of the encryption decision
host_finding_vm_pool_unencrypted.implication: Every guest virtual disk, including lab-hermes-manual-r1/disk.qcow2, is stored on a raw unencrypted partition. Guest-level LUKS is therefore the only control protecting guest data at rest on this host. This matters directly for Gate 3, which writes real provider and bot credentials into the guest profile .env.
host_finding_vm_pool_unencrypted.what_luks_does_not_protect: While the guest is running, host root can read guest memory and the operator-typed passphrase path; guest encryption protects data at rest, not a running guest on a compromised host.
host_finding_vm_pool_unencrypted.action_taken: None. Recorded for the encryption decision and for the Gate 3 threat model.

scope_change_no_guest_encryption.decision: The Gate 2 fixture will be installed WITHOUT LUKS2 encryption.
scope_change_no_guest_encryption.decided_by: user, in response to the agent's finding that the VM pool sits on an unencrypted partition
consequences_accepted: Gate 2 becomes a REDUCED profile: encryption-related acceptance is not exercised.
The guest .env credentials planned for Gate 3 would sit on an unencrypted guest disk, on the raw unencrypted partition /dev/nvme1n1p4.
cryptsetup keyslot/token inspection is NOT_APPLICABLE for this fixture.
The optional TPM/PCR7 no-input boot profile becomes structurally impossible on this fixture (there is no LUKS volume to bind a token to).
Gate 2 must not be cited as evidence for the encrypted-storage path; that path stays unverified.
not_weakened_by_this_decision: A dedicated /home/hermes filesystem of >=20 GiB remains required: every manual helper begins with 'mountpoint -q /home/hermes' and stops otherwise.
SELinux enforcing, rootless Podman, the offline worker and the pinned transport are unchanged.
scope_change_no_guest_encryption.mitigation_available: Host-level encryption of the libvirt images pool is a separate, unaddressed finding recorded in host_finding_vm_pool_unencrypted.

risk_refinement.gate2: No meaningful loss. Gate 2 is credential-free: the guest holds an OS, the profile scripts, container images and an empty .env. Unencrypted is a reasonable choice for this gate.
risk_refinement.gate3: The calculus changes once real provider/bot credentials are written to the profile .env. The realistic lab risk is not theft of the host but that a qcow2 is a copyable file: the retention policy itself plans to preserve the disk on failure, and images get snapshotted and backed up. Unencrypted, each copy is a plaintext credential store.
risk_refinement.limits_of_guest_luks: Guest LUKS protects data at rest only. It does not protect against a compromised host, because host root can read a running guest's memory.
risk_refinement.better_option_if_wanted: Encrypt the host pool (/var/lib/libvirt/images is currently raw /dev/nvme1n1p4). One host-boot unlock covers every guest with no per-guest passphrase prompts. Separate host-change project requiring its own approval.

host_pool_encryption.detail: Host images-pool encryption was requested, then withdrawn before any planning artifact or change was produced. Only read-only reconnaissance was performed: pool paths, fstab entry for /dev/nvme1n1p4, and free space on the encrypted /var were inspected. Nothing was encrypted, moved, unmounted, reformatted or wiped.
host_pool_encryption.note_for_gate3: G3-PRE remains open but the encryption options are now declined. The working assumption is option (a): accept unencrypted storage and use short-lived, revocable, spend-capped lab credentials, treating any qcow2 copy as sensitive. Confirm at Gate 3.

gate3_precondition.requirement: Before Gate 3 provisions any real provider or bot credential, the credential-at-rest decision must be made explicitly: (a) accept unencrypted guest storage with short-lived, revocable, spend-capped lab credentials and prompt revocation; (b) give this fixture guest LUKS (reinstall or in-place encryption); or (c) encrypt the host images pool.
gate3_precondition.status: OPEN — must be resolved before Gate 3 starts
gate3_precondition.why: Gate 2 is credential-free, so this is not a Gate 2 blocker. It becomes one the moment real tokens exist.

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: Refused with 'no SSH public key' when run under sudo.
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: sudo resets HOME to /root, so the default key path resolved to /root/.local/state/hermes-manual-lab/id_ed25519.pub. The same trap had already been handled in gate2-create-fixture.sh via SUDO_USER, but was not applied here.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Resolve the invoking user's home through SUDO_USER; add GATE2_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_FILE; the error now names the path it tried.
defects_found_and_fixed.regression_guard: Verified twice: succeeds via $HOME as a normal user, and succeeds with HOME=/nonexistent when SUDO_USER is set (simulating sudo).
defects_found_and_fixed.note: Second occurrence of the sudo-HOME class of mistake in this gate; both instances are recorded.

defects_found_and_fixed.cause: Correct fail-closed behaviour after F-01 prevented the ISO from being built.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: No code change needed; recorded because the refusal was the right outcome, not a fault.
defects_found_and_fixed.note: The scoped grant was already live, and the wrapper declined rather than restarting the VM with no media.

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: After attaching the kickstart ISO and restarting, the guest booted to 'BdsDxe: No bootable option or device was found.' The domain's sda cdrom had no <source>.

evidence.dvd_owner_after_event: qemu:qemu (libvirt dynamic ownership, so it HAD been attached)
evidence.guest_console: UEFI boot manager, no bootable device

defects_found_and_fixed.cause: NOT PROVEN. The installer ran normally for a long session before this, and no eject command appears anywhere in the record. The most likely mechanism is that the live installer's device probing opened the tray, and the subsequent `virsh attach-disk ... --config` persisted that empty-tray state into the domain configuration. Stated as a hypothesis, not a finding.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: The granted wrapper is now idempotent and verifies its own preconditions: it ensures the installer media occupies the sda tray (insert/update as needed), ensures the kickstart ISO is attached on the SATA bus (the controller the installer demonstrably read), verifies qemu can read both files, refuses if either is not root-owned, and only then restarts the guest.
defects_found_and_fixed.also_fixed: The kickstart ISO had been auto-attached by libvirt on the SCSI bus; it is now attached explicitly on SATA alongside the installer media.
defects_found_and_fixed.residual_risk: If the installer opens the tray again mid-install, the media would be missing during the run. The unattended install is much shorter than the interactive session, and screenshots are being used to monitor it.
defects_found_and_fixed.why_recorded: A guest that cannot boot is exactly the kind of failure the record must capture, including the part that is unexplained.

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: The corrected wrapper refused: 'Fedora-Server-dvd-...iso is not root-owned'.
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: My check required root ownership, but libvirt's dynamic_ownership chowns a domain's disk and CD media to the qemu user while it runs. The media is legitimately qemu:qemu (modes 644 and 640).
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Accept root OR qemu ownership, and enforce what actually matters: readable by the qemu user, and not group/world-writable so no unprivileged human can swap the media. Also prints an explicit verification line.
defects_found_and_fixed.verification: Exercised against the real media: both accepted (owner=qemu, not group/world-writable). Separately proven it still catches a genuinely world-writable file.
defects_found_and_fixed.note: Third defect in my own lab scripts this gate (F-01, F-03, F-04); all were fail-closed, none caused data loss.

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: Three consecutive virsh calls failed with 'authentication failed: access denied by policy'.
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: NOT PROVEN; transient. Retried seconds later and read-only access worked again.
defects_found_and_fixed.action: Recorded rather than attributed. Monitoring therefore retries on transient connection failure instead of treating one failure as a verdict.
defects_found_and_fixed.note: Distinguished from a real permission change deliberately: claiming a cause here would be a guess.

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: Anaconda found the OEMDRV kickstart but rejected it: 'An error occurred during reading the kickstart file: Unrecognized arguments:' and the installer terminated.
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: PROVEN with a real validator, not guessed: pykickstart does not support backslash line continuation. The trailing backslash on the `user` directive was parsed as an extra positional argument, and the following option line became an unknown command.
defects_found_and_fixed.validation_tool: pykickstart 3.78 installed into an ephemeral /tmp venv via `python3 -m venv` (a userspace aid; no host package was installed or changed). It reproduced the installer's error exactly, at the same two lines.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: The user directive is now a single line, with a comment explaining why it must stay that way.
defects_found_and_fixed.verification: ksvalidator reports the fixed file clean (exit 0). The guard was then proven by reinstating the defect: exit 2 with the same 'unrecognized arguments' error.
defects_found_and_fixed.positive_finding: The OEMDRV delivery mechanism WORKED: Anaconda located and read the kickstart from the second CD-ROM. The failure was in the file, not the transport.
defects_found_and_fixed.self_service_improvement: The generator now stores the password hash (0600 root) and accepts --reuse-hash, and a second granted wrapper rebuilds the ISO from the repo template with no prompt, so kickstart fixes no longer need the operator.
defects_found_and_fixed.grant_scope_note: The rebuild wrapper reads the template from the repo checkout recorded in /etc/hermes-gate2/repo-path, so whoever can edit that checkout can change the install media. Intentional for this lab; acceptable only because the fixture is disposable and credential-free.

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: Intermittent 'authentication failed: access denied by policy' when connecting as the login user.
defects_found_and_fixed.measurement: 8 successes and 2 failures in 10 attempts over 30 seconds, with an active seat0 session, a single healthy virtqemud and world-accessible control sockets.
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: NOT PROVEN (would need polkit logs). Recorded as intermittent and unexplained.
defects_found_and_fixed.workaround: A granted root-side observation wrapper (lab/gate2-observe.sh) was written to remove the dependency entirely; it is NOT yet deployed because retry-wrapper observation proved sufficient and each deployment costs the operator a command. Retries are used meanwhile.

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: setup-ssh-key-only.sh rejected the arguments with 'Specify valid --interface and --zone'; firewall_policy also failed with zone_services=none.
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: firewall-cmd --get-active-zones prints 'FedoraServer (default)' in this version, and the annotated string was passed through as the zone name.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Resolve the zone from the interface (firewall-cmd --get-zone-of-interface) with --get-default-zone as fallback, then strip any annotation.
defects_found_and_fixed.verification: Re-run: zone=FedoraServer, ssh_helper_rc=0, ssh_key_only=PASS, firewall_policy=PASS with services 'dhcpv6-client ssh'.

defects_found_and_fixed.symptom: avc_denials reported UNVERIFIED on a host with auditd active and no denials.
defects_found_and_fixed.cause: ausearch exits non-zero when it finds nothing; the code treated that as 'could not read the audit log'.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Treat '<no matches>' as PASS (zero denials), rc=0 with output as FAIL, and only a genuine read failure as UNVERIFIED. Matches the logic already used in m02/m04.
